q: The cut-off time for an equity fund subscription with applicable NAV of the same day is:
e: For equity-oriented schemes, the cut-off time is 3:00 PM. Applications received before 3 PM with funds available get same-day NAV.

q: The cut-off time for liquid fund subscriptions is:
e: Liquid fund subscription cut-off is 1:30 PM. This is to align with banking hours and same-day deployment.

q: For applicable NAV in liquid funds, in addition to the cut-off, what other condition must be met?
o: Funds must be realized in scheme account before cut-off
e: Funds must be CREDITED to the scheme account before cut-off — not just application receipt. This applies to all subscriptions (post-2020 SEBI rule).

q: For equity schemes, the maximum Total Expense Ratio (TER) on the first ₹500 crore of AUM is:
e: For equity schemes, TER on the first ₹500 cr is 2.25%. Subsequent slabs reduce gradually with higher AUM.

q: TER for direct plans is __ regular plans.
e: Direct plans have lower TER because they exclude distributor commission, leading to higher returns over time.

q: NAV of a mutual fund scheme is calculated as:
o: (Total assets − Total liabilities) / number of units
e: NAV = (Net Assets) / Outstanding Units, where Net Assets = Total assets − Total liabilities (including expenses payable).

q: NAV must be published by the AMC:
e: AMCs must declare NAV every business day on AMFI website by 11 PM (and on their own website).

q: Exit load collected by a mutual fund is:
o: Retained by the AMC as fee income
e: Exit load is credited to the scheme — it benefits remaining unitholders, not the AMC.

q: TER includes which of the following?
o: Management fees, marketing, custodian, RTA, audit fees
e: TER covers all recurring scheme expenses — management fees, custodian, RTA, marketing, audit, trustee fees, etc. Brokerage/STT are excluded from TER limit.

q: Mutual funds are allowed to charge differential exit loads based on the amount of investment.
e: Differential exit loads based on investment amount are NOT allowed. Exit load must be uniform across all unitholders within a scheme on a given date.

q: For an equity scheme with AUM of ₹2,000 crore, the additional expense allowed for inflows from B-30 cities is:
e: AMCs can charge an additional expense of up to 0.30 bps for B-30 city inflows, subject to certain conditions on retail investor share.

q: NAV is applied based on:
o: Time of fund realization in scheme account
Whichever is later: application time or fund realization
e: Both conditions must be met before cut-off — application AND fund realization. Whichever happens later determines NAV applicability.

q: Direct plan TER is __ regular plan:
e: Lower — no distributor commission.

q: TER on first ₹500 cr AUM (equity scheme):
Exit load goes to:
e: Credited to the scheme.

q: For a debt scheme with an NAV in the range of ₹10–₹100, NAV is typically rounded to:
e: For debt schemes (and money market / liquid schemes), NAVs are computed and disclosed up to 4 decimal places to capture small daily accruals accurately.

q: For an equity scheme, NAV is typically disclosed up to:
e: Equity scheme NAVs are typically disclosed up to 2 decimal places (sometimes 4). Debt schemes go to 4 decimals due to smaller daily accruals.

q: The B-30 incentive (additional expense up to 0.30% of additional AUM) is permitted for inflows from:
e: B-30 = Beyond Top 30 cities. AMCs can charge up to 0.30 bps additional expense for inflows from B-30 cities to incentivise distribution outside metros.

q: For a Liquid Fund, NAV is calculated:
o: For each calendar day (including weekends and holidays)
e: Liquid fund NAVs are computed for EACH CALENDAR DAY (including weekends and holidays) — since they hold money market instruments that accrue interest daily.

q: For an equity-oriented mutual fund scheme, what is the cut-off time for redemption?
e: Redemption cut-off for equity and debt (other than liquid) is 3:00 PM. Same-day NAV if before, next business day NAV if after.

q: For purchase in an equity scheme of any amount, the applicable NAV is the NAV of the day:
o: When funds are realized and available for utilisation before cut-off
e: Post Feb 2021, applicable NAV is when funds are credited to the scheme account before cut-off, regardless of size of investment.

q: NAV indicates how much money can be generated per unit of mutual fund in case the scheme is:
e: NAV represents the per-unit value of the scheme — i.e., what each unitholder would theoretically receive if all securities were liquidated and liabilities settled.

q: For valuation of debt securities for mutual fund NAV, the SEBI-approved valuation agencies are:
e: CRISIL and ICRA are the SEBI-approved valuation agencies for debt securities used in mutual fund schemes.

q: NAV of a scheme is disclosed on the website of:
e: NAV is disclosed daily by 11 PM on the AMC website AND on AMFI website.

q: Investors bought 20 crore units of a scheme at ₹10 each (mobilizing ₹200 crore). ₹140 crore is in equities; ₹60 crore in bank deposits. Interest/dividend accrued: ₹8 crore. Scheme expenses payable: ₹4 crore. Calculate NAV per unit.
e: Net Assets = 140 + 60 + 8 - 4 = ₹204 cr. NAV = ₹204 cr ÷ 20 cr units = ₹10.20.

q: Maximum Total Expense Ratio chargeable in case of Index Funds is:
e: Index funds and ETFs are capped at 1% TER under SEBI regulations — given their passive nature and lower management cost.

q: Mutual fund dividends (IDCW) can be paid only out of:
o: Distributable surplus generated by the scheme
e: Dividends/IDCW can be paid only out of distributable surplus — i.e., realised gains and accumulated income, NOT from unit capital or unrealised gains.

q: A scheme has total assets of ₹500 crore, total liabilities (including expenses payable) of ₹8 crore, and 25 crore units outstanding. NAV is:
An investor invests ₹1,000 per month via SIP for 3 months. Unit NAVs were ₹10, ₹12.50, and ₹8 respectively. Average NAV per unit acquired (Rupee Cost Average) is approximately:
e: Units: 100, 80, 125 → total 305 units for ₹3,000 → Avg cost = 3000/305 ≈ ₹9.84 (~₹9.80). Lower than the simple average of NAVs (₹10.17) — illustrating Rupee Cost Averaging benefit.

q: A scheme distributed dividend of ₹2 per unit. NAV before dividend was ₹15. Ex-dividend NAV is:
e: Ex-dividend NAV = NAV − dividend = 15 − 2 = ₹13. NAV drops by the dividend amount on the ex-dividend date.

q: An investor buys at NAV ₹50, redeems at NAV ₹62 with 1% exit load. Effective redemption price is:
e: Exit load 1% on ₹62 = ₹0.62 deducted. Investor receives ₹62 − ₹0.62 = ₹61.38.

q: For an equity scheme, AUM ₹1,500 crore. SEBI TER slab structure: 2.25% on first ₹500 cr, 2.00% on next ₹250 cr, 1.75% on next ₹1,250 cr (relevant range). Approximate weighted TER cap is closer to:
Investor invests ₹5 lakh in a debt fund. Exit load of 1% if redeemed within 1 year. Exits after 8 months at ₹5.4 lakh value. Redemption proceeds (before tax):
A liquid fund returns 6% annualized. Daily approximate compounded return per day:
e: Approx. (1.06)^(1/365) − 1 ≈ 0.000164 = 0.0164% per day. Liquid funds accrue daily — small but consistent.

q: Scheme expenses for the period: management fee ₹4 cr, marketing ₹1 cr, custody ₹0.5 cr, audit ₹0.2 cr, brokerage ₹0.8 cr. TER is computed on:
e: TER excludes brokerage and STT. Recurring expenses (management, marketing, custody, RTA, audit) total ₹5.7 cr counted in TER.

q: A scheme that charges TER higher than the SEBI-prescribed slab is:
e: TER must always remain within SEBI-prescribed slabs. Exceeding is a regulatory violation. The slabs depend on AUM and scheme type.

q: Heads of expenses that can be charged to a mutual fund scheme are specified by:
e: SEBI specifies the heads of expenses that can be charged to a scheme (management fees, custodian, RTA, audit, marketing, legal, etc.). AMC cannot charge other heads.

q: For a segregated portfolio (side-pocket) created on a credit event, the NAV is:
o: Computed separately, with the affected security carved out at carrying value or fair value
e: When a segregated portfolio is created, units are split. Main portfolio continues with healthy assets; segregated portfolio is computed separately with the affected security at fair value (often heavily marked down).

q: For an equity scheme with AUM of ₹3,000 crore, the SEBI TER slab structure applies:
o: 2.25% on first ₹500cr, 2.00% on next ₹250cr, 1.75% on next ₹1,250cr, 1.60% on next ₹3,000cr, etc.
e: SEBI TER slabs (equity): 2.25% / 2.00% / 1.75% / 1.60% / 1.50% / 1.05% on incremental AUM tranches. Larger funds have lower weighted TER.

q: GST on the management fee is:
o: Charged within the TER (i.e., included in scheme expenses)
e: GST on management fees and other applicable scheme expenses is charged within the TER — investors bear it indirectly. Not charged separately.

q: Brokerage and Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on the scheme's portfolio transactions are:
o: Excluded from TER (charged additionally to the scheme)
e: Brokerage and STT are EXCLUDED from the TER cap. They are charged additionally to the scheme as transaction costs — but capped at 12 bps for cash-market and 5 bps for derivatives.

q: For inflows from B-30 cities into open-ended equity-oriented schemes (excluding ETFs/Index Funds), the additional expense allowed is:
o: Up to 0.30% of AUM (incremental from B-30) — for retail investors only
e: B-30 incentive: up to 0.30% of B-30 incremental AUM. Applies only to retail investor inflows; reversed if redeemed within 1 year.

q: If the B-30 inflow investor redeems within 1 year, the B-30 incentive amount must be:
e: If B-30 investor redeems within 1 year, the additional expense incentive previously claimed by AMC must be clawed back. Prevents abuse for short-term gains.

q: For a Liquid Fund, NAV must be calculated:
o: Each calendar day (including weekends and holidays)
e: Liquid funds calculate NAV for EACH CALENDAR DAY since they hold money market instruments accruing interest daily. Other funds calculate only on business days.

q: The Maximum TER for an Index Fund / ETF (any AUM) is:
e: Index Funds and ETFs are capped at 1% TER given their passive, low-management-cost nature.

q: For a Fund of Funds (FoF), the SEBI TER cap is:
o: 2.25% (combining FoF expenses + underlying scheme weighted expenses)
e: FoF TER cap is 2.25%, computed as FoF's own TER + weighted average of underlying scheme TERs. Prevents double layering.

q: NAV decimal places are:
o: 2 for equity, 4 for debt/liquid (to capture daily accruals accurately)
e: Equity NAVs typically rounded to 2 decimals. Debt/Liquid funds rounded to 4 decimals to capture small daily interest accruals accurately.

q: For a scheme that has charged additional B-30 expense, the disclosure requirement is:
o: Disclosed in factsheet/SID/AMC website with B-30 AUM details
e: AMC must disclose B-30 AUM and the additional expense charged separately in the factsheet, SID, and on the website — for transparency.

q: Exit load credited to the scheme:
o: Goes back to scheme NAV (benefits remaining unitholders)
e: Exit load is credited to the SCHEME (not the AMC) — directly benefits remaining unitholders by adding to scheme NAV. Aligns interests.

q: B-30 incentive for retail investor inflows from beyond top-30 cities is up to ___ of the additional AUM:
e: B-30 incentive: up to 0.30% (30 bps) of additional AUM from B-30 retail investors. Clawed back if redeemed within 1 year.

q: A scheme's NAV declaration deadline (across the industry) is:
o: 11 PM same business day on AMFI website
e: NAV must be uploaded to AMFI website by 11 PM on the same business day. Liquid funds calculate NAV for every calendar day.

q: For an equity-oriented scheme of any amount, applicable NAV is the NAV of:
o: The day funds are credited and available for utilisation in the scheme account before cut-off
e: Post Feb 2021, NAV applicability for any amount in equity is based on FUNDS REALISATION before cut-off — not application size. Equalises treatment across investors.

q: For a Liquid Fund subscription, the cut-off time is:
e: Liquid fund subscription cut-off: 1:30 PM. Funds must be available for utilisation before cut-off for previous day NAV applicability.

q: For an equity scheme of AUM ₹2,500 crore, the SEBI TER cap weighted across slabs is approximately:
When the cut-off time and fund realisation work in tandem, the applicable NAV depends on:
o: Whichever is later: application time OR fund realisation
e: Both conditions must be satisfied before cut-off — application AND fund realisation. Whichever is LATER determines NAV.
